<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec (when written): `SPEC.md`.

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or issues.
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5-1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission". Reasoning effort per role is set in `SPEC.md`.
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

17→The observatory attaches to missions started from any terminal on this machine (it watches `~/.factory/sessions/` and tails each new session file as it grows), replays finished ones from the same files, and can also host a mission itself (it spawns `droid exec --mission` and consumes the JSON-RPC event stream, which adds the control channel). Attach is the primary live mode; hosting is the secondary path. It never copies the event data into a second source of truth: every lane entry is a view over the raw JSONL line it came from.
18→
19→A mission is not complete when the workers stop. It is complete when the gate is green and the merge has happened.

21→## 2. Delivery model
22→
23→This section defines the units the board shows. Everything else follows from it.
24→
25→- **A mission is a business feature: the unit that ships.** For this project, v1 of the observatory. A mission ends in **one PR into `main`**, outcome-sized, with the evidence attached. The full attested CI runs on that PR; CD runs from `main`.
26→- **Milestones are internal iterations**, not shippable. Each milestone runs in its own worktree and is integrated into a **`mission/<name>` branch**, the mission's interface to `main`. Fast checks (tests, lint, the gate command) run on that branch to keep it healthy. Nothing on it is shippable or pretends to be.
27→- **The mission branch is short-lived by construction.** It dies at the merge. That is what keeps it from becoming a long-lived `dev` branch.
28→- **Features** are the orchestrator's work items inside a milestone. Workers build them, validators judge them, and metrics are computed at feature granularity, then rolled up to the milestone and the mission.
29→- **The fix loop after CI red reopens the mission on its branch.** It does not open a new PR. The same PR goes green or stays red.
30→
31→On the board: **cards are milestones**; the gate group in lane 8 is the mission's one PR; lane 6 is integration into `mission/<name>`; lane 8 is the PR.
32→
33→**Models per role** (decision D-006; `ai/RULES.md` rule 19): orchestrator `claude-fable-5-1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`. Reasoning effort per role is declared in the spec. A change of model is a decision file.
34→
35→## 3. Problem
36→
37→Mission Control (CLI and Factory App) shows progress, workers, and a log. It does not show:
38→
39→- the mission's full life, including what happens after the workers stop (PR, CI, attestations, deploy, red builds that need a fix);
40→- where time goes: active work versus waiting on a human, waiting on validation, waiting on merge, rework after a blocking finding, retries and conflicts;
41→- what each role and model consumed, so that model and reasoning-effort choices can be compared with real numbers;
42→- a single place to act when the mission needs a human: approve, answer, redirect, merge.
43→
44→Running missions without that view means managing agents blind on the two dimensions that matter most for an engineering organization: flow and cost.
45→
46→## 4. Goals
47→
48→1. Show every milestone of a mission across the nine lanes defined in section 7, live and in replay, with features visible inside each card.
49→2. Show per card: validation state (red/green), current agent, gate state, and a Details view with review notes, validation criteria, commits, and raw event links.
50→3. Let the human act from the board: pause/resume the orchestrator, send instructions, answer escalations, approve, mark a feature complete or skipped, and merge the PR when policy says a human merges.
51→4. Measure cycle time, waste by cause, mission overhead, and bottlenecks per feature, per milestone, per role, and per mission.
52→5. Measure cost: tokens per sub-droid, converted to Factory Standard Credits when the stream exposes them, otherwise money via a dated price table that every displayed cost references.
53→6. Treat CI red on the mission PR as a counted rework loop: reopen the mission on its branch, loop the affected card back into the Workers lane, keep the same PR.

58→- Multi-user or server deployment. v1 is a single-user desktop app reading local data and the user's own GitHub access.
59→- Writing to Factory's hosted API beyond what the local `droid` process already does.
60→- Editing code or reviewing diffs inside the app. It links out to the worktree, commit, or PR.

93→## 8. Board model
94→
95→**Card = one milestone.** The milestone is the spec phase: the orchestrator plans it, workers build its features in a worktree, validators judge it, and it integrates into `mission/<name>`. Each card lists its features with their individual state, and metrics roll up feature → milestone → mission.
96→
97→A card moves left to right. Its position is the lane where its most recent open activity is. The Details view shows the full history across lanes.
98→
99→**Gate group.** Lane 8 holds one group per mission: the mission PR. All cards of the mission share that gate state; the badge sits on the group. Until the PR exists, lane 8 shows the mission branch with its fast-check status as a pre-gate placeholder.
100→
101→**Fix loop.** When CI goes red on the mission PR, the observatory reopens the mission on `mission/<name>` with a cycle tagged `fix` on the milestone(s) whose features the fix touches. Those cards are drawn with a loop arrow back into lane 3. The PR stays the same. The loop is counted as rework in lane 9.
102→
103→**Mission completion.** Mission state is `complete` only when the PR is merged with CI green. Until then it is `planning`, `building`, `validating`, `at gate`, or `fixing`.

201→## 10. Metric definitions
202→
203→### 10.1 Time states
204→
205→Each feature, at every instant, is in exactly one time state:
206→
207→| State | Definition |
208→|---|---|
209→| **Active** | A worker, validator, or orchestrator is doing something for the feature: tool call in flight or model generating. |
210→| **Waiting on human** | A question or approval is open and nobody is acting (lane 7 open, lanes 2–6 idle for this feature). Sub-causes: *question*, *permission*, *waiting on merge* (checks green, policy requires a human, nobody has merged). |
211→| **Waiting on validation** | Work is done, validator not started. |
212→| **Retry and failure** | Time in tool errors, `hook.blocked`, re-runs of the same command, and conflict resolution. |
213→| **Idle, queued** | Feature is planned and ready but blocked behind another feature (WIP limit, dependency, no free worker). A bottleneck signal. |
214→| **Idle, unscheduled** | Feature exists but nothing is scheduled and nothing is blocking it. Not a bottleneck signal. |
215→
216→Rework is not a separate time state. It is a window (10.2) that overlays active, retry, and waiting time.
217→
218→### 10.2 Rework windows
219→
220→A **rework window** opens at a blocking signal and closes at its resolution event, per signal:
221→
222→| Opens | Closes |
223→|---|---|
224→| `finding.blocking` | `rework.resolved` |
225→| `qa.scenario.failed` | `qa.scenario.passed` for the same scenario |
226→| `integration.conflict` | `integration.conflict_resolved` |
227→| `check.failed` (mission PR) | `check.passed` for the same check |
228→
229→Overlapping windows on the same feature merge into one. A window with no closing event stays open until mission end and is reported as unresolved.
230→
231→- **Rework time** = active time inside rework windows.
232→- **First-pass active time** = active time outside any rework window.
233→
234→This bounds rework so that legitimate new work after a fix is not counted as waste.
235→
236→### 10.3 Mission overhead
237→
238→Orchestrator time before the first `feature.defined`, replanning time not attributable to one feature, and `context.compacted` recovery belong to no card. They are reported as **mission overhead**, a separate line in lane 9, never apportioned silently. An optional explicit apportionment (equal split across features) can be switched on for comparisons and is labeled as such.
239→
240→### 10.4 Derived measures
241→
242→- **Cycle time** (feature) = `feature.defined` → feature's last `task.done` with validation green and integrated. **Cycle time** (milestone) = `milestone.defined` → `milestone.completed`. **Cycle time** (mission) = `intent.created` → `pr.merged` (human or policy) with CI green. Stage cycle times are computed per lane.
243→- **Waste** = total elapsed − first-pass active time, split by cause: waiting on human (question, permission, merge), waiting on validation, rework, retry and failure, idle queued, idle unscheduled. Mission overhead is reported next to waste, not inside it. Reported per feature, per milestone, and per role.
244→- **Bottleneck** = lane or role with the highest sum of waiting plus queued time across features in the window, and the lane with the highest WIP relative to its throughput.
245→- **Fix loops** = count of `fix` cycles per milestone and per mission.
246→
247→### 10.5 Cost
248→
249→- Token counts are taken from `usage.reported` events per session (input, output, cache read, cache write when available).
250→- If the stream reports Factory Standard Credits, credits are the primary unit.
251→- Otherwise cost = Σ tokens × price per model and token class, from the **price table**: a dated config file (`~/.droid-observatory/prices/<YYYY-MM-DD>.toml`). The board always shows the date of the table it used, and a mission keeps the table it started with unless the user re-prices it explicitly.
252→- Cost is shown next to waste so that a slow, cheap model and a fast, expensive one can be compared on the same panel.

340→## 12. Technology options and recommendation
341→
342→Constraint: Rust. Preference: Tauri 2. Needs: data-dense board, live updates, charts, markdown and video rendering in Details, long-lived subprocess management, SQLite.
343→
344→| Option | Pros | Cons |
345→|---|---|---|
346→| **A. Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust, CSR via Trunk)** | Single language; shared serde types between core and UI with no bindings; fine-grained reactivity suits a live board; webview gives markdown, video, CSS layout for free. | Charting ecosystem thinner than JS; WASM/Trunk toolchain adds build steps; smaller community. **Droids have far less Leptos in their training than React or Svelte**, so worker rework on UI tasks is likely higher. **The WASM/Trunk toolchain inside a Mission is a new failure mode** (toolchain install, target, dev server) that validators may struggle to diagnose. |
347→| B. Tauri 2 + Dioxus | Same single-language benefit; React-like ergonomics; growing fast. | Dioxus also ships its own desktop renderer, which blurs the "why Tauri" story; same training-data and toolchain concerns as A. |
348→| C. Tauri 2 + TypeScript (Svelte or React) | Richest charting and UI libraries; fastest to a polished UI; best-known stack for Droids. | Two languages; types must be generated (ts-rs/specta) and kept in sync; the user's stated preference is Rust. |
349→| D. iced (native) | Pure Rust, no webview, small binary, Elm architecture fits an event-driven board. | Markdown, video, and rich text are weak; complex layouts cost more effort; no Tauri plugin ecosystem (keyring, updater, tray). |
350→| E. egui (native, immediate mode) | Trivial live updates and plots (egui_plot); excellent for dashboards. | Looks like a tool, not an app; text-heavy Details view (review notes, markdown) is awkward; accessibility and theming limited. |
351→
352→**Recommendation: Option A, Tauri 2 + Leptos, with M1 as an explicit go/no-go.**
353→
354→Reasoning: the hard part of this product is `observatory-core` (ingest, mapping, metrics), not the UI. Keeping the UI in Rust means the metric types, lane mapping, and event model are used directly in the view with no translation layer, which is where drift and bugs would otherwise appear. The webview covers the rich-content needs (markdown findings, QA video, PR rendering) that native options handle poorly. Charting is the one real gap; lane 9 needs stacked bars and timelines, achievable as SVG from Leptos signals, with a JS chart library as a documented escape hatch.
355→
356→**Go/no-go criterion (evaluated at M1 completion):** the board renders the M0 replay (all nine lanes, cards positioned correctly, Details timeline open) with **at most 3 worker sessions of rework** after the first scrutiny pass, and the Trunk/WASM build succeeds from a clean checkout with the documented command. If either fails, switch to Option C for M2 onward, keeping `observatory-core` unchanged; the Tauri command boundary is designed to make that swap possible. (Threshold of 3 agreed 2026-10-22; may be adjusted at planning time.)

431→## Appendix B: Glossary
432→
433→- **Mission**: a business feature, the unit that ships. One PR into `main`.
434→- **Mission branch**: `mission/<name>`, the mission's interface to `main`. Short-lived; dies at the merge.
435→- **Milestone**: an internal iteration inside a mission; runs in its own worktree; integrates into the mission branch; one card.
436→- **Feature**: the orchestrator's work item inside a milestone; the granularity at which metrics are computed.
437→- **Sub-droid**: any agent session spawned for the mission: orchestrator, worker, scrutiny validator, user-testing validator.
438→- **Integration**: landing a milestone worktree on the mission branch, with fast checks. Not a merge in the gate sense.
439→- **Gate**: the mission PR into `main`, merged by a human or by policy, triggering attested CI and possibly CD.
440→- **Fix cycle**: a mission cycle tagged `fix` on the affected milestone(s) after CI red at the gate. Same branch, same PR.
441→- **Rework window**: the span from a blocking signal to its resolution on one feature.
442→- **First-pass active time**: active time outside any rework window.
443→- **Mission overhead**: orchestrator time attributable to no feature; reported separately.
444→- **Waste**: elapsed time that is not first-pass active time, split by cause.

{"file":"docs/decisions/D-010-telemetry-contract.md","result":"1→# D-010: Telemetry contract for the Grafana Cloud stack
2→
3→**Date:** 2026-10-22
4→**Status:** accepted (owner-provided contract; code in the telemetry milestone)
5→
6→## Context
7→
8→D-004 chose Grafana Cloud over OTLP and sketched metric names with a wide attribute list
9→(`feature`, `session`, `class`, `unit`, `price_table`, a gauge for active agents). The owner
10→has provisioned the stack and set the operating constraints below. Cardinality on Grafana
11→Cloud is billed per active series, so the attribute set is the contract that matters.
12→
13→## Decision
14→
15→- **Transport:** OTLP over HTTP (`http/protobuf`) to
16→  `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp` (`/v1/metrics`, `/v1/traces`,
17→  `/v1/logs`). The endpoint is not a secret and lives in `config/observatory.example.toml`.
18→- **Credential:** the full `Authorization=Basic …` header value is read at runtime from the
19→  macOS keychain item with service `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` and account = the
20→  current user. It is never written to config, the store or logs. If the item is missing,
21→  telemetry stays off and the UI says so (a visible "telemetry: off, no keychain item"
22→  state, not a silent failure). The environment variable `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` is
23→  for CI only (B-002); the app does not read it.
24→- **Resource attributes:** `service.name=droid-observatory` and `service.version` (the
25→  crate version). Nothing else. D-004's `deployment.environment` and `service.namespace`
26→  are dropped.
27→- **Metric attributes (labels):** only from the set `mission`, `milestone`, `role`,
28→  `model`, `cause`. Never a session id, event id, feature id or free text. Anything
29→  that varied by `class`, `unit` or `status` in D-004 becomes part of the metric name
30→  (for example `observatory.tokens.input`, `observatory.cost_usd`) or is not exported.
31→- **Instruments:** counters and histograms only. No per-event gauges;
32→  `observatory.active_agents` is not exported (it stays an in-app view).
33→- **Series budget:** the spec states the exact metric set and the number of active series
34→  the app adds, computed from the label cardinalities, and keeps it **under 200**. The
35→  arithmetic is the spec's (B-017); the shape it must fit is: one mission exporting at a
36→  time, up to 6 milestones, 3 roles, up to 4 models, a closed list of waste causes, and a
37→  histogram costs one series per bucket plus `_sum` and `_count`, so explicit bucket
38→  boundaries are part of the contract.
39→
40→## Alternatives
41→
42→- Keep D-004's attribute list and rely on Grafana's adaptive metrics to aggregate: pays for
43→  the series first, then hides them; rejected.
44→- Export per-feature series: `feature` would be the largest cardinality by far and is
45→  already visible in the app; rejected by the owner.
46→- Read the header from the environment as a fallback in the app: one more place a secret can
47→  leak into a shell history or a log; rejected by the owner.
48→
49→## Consequences
50→
51→- D-004 stays accepted for the choice of backend and the two kinds of telemetry; its
52→  attribute list, resource attributes and the gauge are superseded here.
53→- `config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]` carries the endpoint, the keychain
54→  service name, the allowed label set, the series budget and the revised metric names.
55→- PRD v0.5 §11.4 states the contract. `.env.example` marks the OTLP variables CI-only.
56→- B-017: the spec session computes the series count and names the histogram buckets.
57→"}
